name: Grand Principality of Hungary (the Magyars)
summary: The Magyar tribes who moved from the steppe into the Carpathian basin (the “Conquest”, around 895) under Árpád, raided across Europe until defeated at Lechfeld (955), and became the Christian Kingdom of Hungary in 1000.

location.value: First Etelköz, east of the Carpathians; then the Carpathian basin.
location.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

terrain.value: Open grassland steppe with river valleys.

climate.value: Continental: hot summers and very cold winters.

resources.value: Pasture for horses, sheep and cattle.

disasters.value: Harsh winters (dzud) that killed herds; droughts.

urbanisation.value: Mostly nomadic camps; a few trading towns.

disease.value: Plague and epidemics carried along trade routes.

migration.value: Led by Árpád from Etelköz, the Hungarians crossed the Carpathians around 895, perhaps after a joint attack by the Pechenegs and Bulgarians.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (checked 8 Nov 2026)

economicBase.value: Herding horses, sheep and cattle; tribute and raiding.

tradeRoutes.value: Raids and trade with Western Europe and Byzantium.

wealth.value: Wealth in herds, tribute and plunder.

moneyAndTax.value: Tribute from settled neighbours; little coinage of their own.

inequality.value: Ruling clans above commoner herders and slaves.

governmentType.value: A federation of seven tribes, first led by two chiefs: the kende (Kurszán) and the gyula (Árpád).
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (checked 8 Nov 2026)

keyRulers.value: Árpád, founder of the Árpád dynasty; Grand Prince Géza, who began to consolidate the state.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

succession.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

institutions.value: Clan assemblies and the khan’s household.

stability.value: Seven tribes formed the federation (the “Seven Magyars”); the grand prince’s power seemed to weaken during the raiding years.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

majorWars.value: Raids across Europe; victory at Pressburg (907), after which no western army attacked Hungary for over 100 years; defeat at Lechfeld (955).
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded; skilled horsemanship and metalwork.

openness.value: Open to trade and alliances with settled empires.

religion.value: Steppe beliefs; Christianity spread from the second half of the 900s.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.value: Hungarian (a Uralic language); Old Hungarian runes.

dailyLife.value: Felt tents; meat, milk and fermented mare’s milk.

neighbours.value: East Francia, the First Bulgarian Empire and Great Moravia, which ruled the Carpathian basin when the Hungarians arrived; the Pechenegs to the east.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

outcome.value: Became the Christian Kingdom of Hungary when Stephen I was crowned at Esztergom on Christmas Day 1000 (or 1 January 1001).
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Grand Principality of Hungary (checked 8 Nov 2026)

overallCertainty.value: Known mostly from Byzantine, Chinese, Arab and Persian writers and from archaeology; numbers are estimates.
